title: Coral and the Summer
premise: Coral 'Casper' Pemberton returns to Gullwing Point to keep her late grandfather's lighthouse from being sold, only to find her family expects her to arrive with the fiancé she invented two years ago. She recruits Theo Marsh, a marine biologist studying the reef her grandfather protected, to play the part for one weekend reunion that stretches into the whole summer festival season. As staged dates blur into real intimacy, Casper discovers Theo's research could legally doom the reef—and that her publisher wants her next novel to be a tell-all memoir exposing the town's complicity in a decades-old cover-up her grandfather helped bury. When the truth surfaces at the lantern festival, Casper must choose between the career that saved her from grief and the man who shows her that belonging means being seen, not performing. She burns the memoir draft, testifies informally at the town hearing on Theo's behalf, and stays: the lighthouse saved, the reef protected by the town itself, and a love that no longer needs a script.
about_author: Juniper Villalobos is a former tide-pool docent who writes love stories set in coastal towns that smell like salt and second chances. She lives in a converted boathouse with an opinionated gull named Marguerite.

chapters.title: The Letter That Smelled of Brine
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In her Brooklyn apartment, Casper learns the family trust will sell Gullwing Light unless she attends the summer reunion—and that everyone expects her fiancé. Panic, deflection, and a half-finished novel she's hiding from her editor. Beat: dread disguised as control.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Good Posture
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At a café, she overhears Theo Marsh arguing on the phone about grant funding for his reef survey. On impulse she offers him room, board, and a fiction: play my fiancé for the summer. He laughs, then says yes. Beat: reckless hope.

chapters.title: Driving into the Story We Made Up
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The road trip north; they negotiate the rules of the fake engagement in a diner, and Casper realizes she's enjoying lying. First glimpse of the lighthouse. Beat: the con begins to feel like a gift.

chapters.title: Aunt Bev Knows Everything
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The reunion's first dinner: probing questions, a suspicious aunt, and Theo improvising a proposal story so tender that Casper's chest hurts. He notices her flinch at her grandfather's name. Beat: the audience believes them; so do they, slightly.

chapters.title: What Grandfather Kept Below
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Exploring the lighthouse, she finds her grandfather's hidden logbooks referencing 'the spill' and payments from the cannery. She hides them from Theo. Beat: memory as burden.

chapters.title: Dessert Was the Mistake
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The reunion's final night; a shared slice of plum cake, a dance on the porch, and a kiss staged for the aunts that neither pulls back from. Beat: the fake date becomes too real, exactly as the blurb promised.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions of the Heart
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Morning-after avoidance; she retreats into drafting and emails her editor, who proposes a memoir about her grandfather and the town. Beat: the career that saved everything makes its offer.

chapters.title: The Reef Doesn't Lie
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Casper joins his survey dive; underwater, wordless, she sees the dying coral and his quiet fury. He tells her the contamination matches old cannery records. Beat: intimacy through shared purpose.

chapters.title: Festival of Small Lights
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The town's midsummer festival: paper lanterns, a fortune-teller who reads them both too accurately, and Casper nearly confessing the fake engagement. Beat: the truth pressing at the seams.

chapters.title: The Logbooks in the Lamplight
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He finds the hidden logbooks while repairing a shutter; Casper catches him reading. Their first real fight—about secrets, justice, and whose grief owns the truth. Beat: trust cracks.

chapters.title: Editor's Deadline, Rising Tide
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Her publisher loves the memoir angle and wants the cover-up exposed by festival's end; the advance would buy the lighthouse outright. Beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: What the Aunts Remember
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Aunt Bev, softened by brandy, reveals the cannery paid families to stay silent after the spill—including Grandfather, who kept the money in a locked fund 'for the reef.' Beat: justice outside the law takes shape.

chapters.title: A Date That Isn't One
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They stop pretending for one evening—no audience, no script—and it's the most honest date either has ever had. Beat: falling, admitted only to the reader.

chapters.title: The Fund in Grandfather's Name
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She cracks the locked drawer: the embezzled payments were saved intact, earmarked for restoration. She could hand it to Theo—or to her publisher as the memoir's climax. Beat: the choice sharpening.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. His grant is revoked after an anonymous tip—the cannery's heirs, it turns out, still hold town influence. He decides to leave after the festival. Beat: everything Casper could lose, made concrete.

chapters.title: The Manuscript and the Man
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Theo discovers her memoir draft—his name in it, the fake engagement, everything. He feels used; she feels exposed. The engagement fiction collapses entirely. Beat: the darkest hour.

chapters.title: Low Tide, Bare Feet
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Alone at dawn, she reads her grandfather's last log entry: 'The heart is not a muscle to train. It's a tide. You let it come in.' She deletes the memoir and calls Aunt Bev. Beat: the turn inward.

chapters.title: The Hearing at the Grange Hall
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The town convenes on the reef contamination. Casper arrives uninvited, presents the fund and the logbooks, and speaks not as a Pemberton but as a witness. Beat: justice outside the law, delivered publicly.

chapters.title: Lanterns on the Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Festival's final night: the town votes to restore the reef with the fund; Casper releases a lantern with her grandfather's name on it and finds Theo at the seawall. The apology, and the first honest kiss. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: What She Writes Instead
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She tells her editor the memoir is dead and offers a novel instead—one about a lighthouse, a liar, and a tide. Her agent threatens to walk; she lets him. Beat: choosing the person over the career that saved everything.

chapters.title: The Light Kept Burning
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The lighthouse is saved by the trust's revised terms; Theo's new grant, co-signed by the town, funds the restoration. He asks her—not to stay, but to choose. Beat: love as invitation, not demand.

chapters.title: Coral and the Summer
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Epilogue in September: the first restored coral blooms, the lighthouse lamp is lit by Casper's hand, and the novel's dedication page reads 'For the one who saw clearly at last.' Beat: belonging, finally, without a script.
